ety.text: From on + to, after into. Compare Saterland Frisian antou (“up to”).

senses.d: Arriving upon or on top of (speaking of a physical or metaphorical movement).
ex: My cat just jumped onto the keyboard.
A new drug has just come onto the market.
The thought-police were onto my plans of world domination.

senses.d: Being an onto function with a codomain of (see below).
ex: The exponential function maps the set of real numbers onto the set of positive real numbers.

senses.d: Attaining each of the values in its codomain; having its image equal to its codomain.
ex: Considered as a function on the real numbers, the exponential function is not onto, as it never takes on values less than or equal to zero.

chain.g: [of place] above; over; on the top of; upon

ety.text: Inherited from Middle French sur, from Old French sur, seur, sor, soure, souvre, sovre (“on, upon, over”), from Latin super (“over, on, above”). Doublet of super, a borrowing. Cognate with Old English ofer (“over, above”). More at over.
Inherited from Old Spanish sobre, from Latin super (“above”), from *eks-uper, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰs (“out of”) (Latin ex) and *uperi (“above”), from *upo. Doublet of the borrowed super.

pt:sobre.gl: on; atop; on top of (located on the top surface of)

chain.g: [of place] above; over; on the top of; upon

ety.text: From Old Galician-Portuguese sobre, from Latin super, from *eks-uper, which consists of Proto-Indo-European *eḱs (“out of”) and *uperi. Doublet of the borrowed super. Cognate to Spanish sobre, French sur, Ancient Greek ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”) and English over, super and sur-.
